title: Draft a progress review summary and employer email
context: James Rowe is a Data Academy skills coach with {{fact:dlv_rowe_caseload}} learners. He held a progress review with Judith Lewis (DA4, Redwood Logistics) on 30 October; she was rated Red because her OTJ has fallen behind. It is late afternoon and he still needs to write up the review and email her line manager.
goal: Use Copilot to draft an accurate coach summary for Judith's review and a polite, specific email to her line manager asking for protected OTJ time — then check both against the Coach Handbook.
task_steps: Open Judith Lewis's progress review record in the Learner Files library (Data Academy / Redwood Logistics Ltd).
Ask Copilot to summarise her review history and current OTJ position.
Ask Copilot to draft a coach summary with 3 SMART targets in plain English.
Check the RAG rating against the thresholds in the Skills Coach Handbook.
In Outlook, ask Copilot to draft an email to the line manager requesting about 5 hours a week of protected learning time, referencing the employer OTJ guide.
Edit the tone and facts, and compare your draft with the actual email thread with Redwood Logistics.
sample_prompts: Summarise /Progress Review - LRN20533 Judith Lewis: OTJ position, RAG and the trend across her reviews.
Using the Skills Coach Handbook, explain why Judith is rated Red and what I must do next.
Draft a 150-word coach summary for Judith's review with three SMART targets. Plain English, no personal details.
Draft a friendly email to Judith's line manager asking for a protected weekly study slot of around 5 hours. Attach the off-the-job training guide for employers.
success_criteria: Summary quotes OTJ logged vs expected correctly and states Red (under 78%).
Escalation to the delivery manager within 5 working days is identified.
Email is specific (hours per week, start date, next check-in) and professional.
No health or sensitive personal data in the outputs.
trainer_notes: Good first scenario for coaches who are less confident with Copilot. Emphasise checking numbers against the source and removing sensitive detail. The real email thread shows a model answer.

title: Find at-risk learners in the caseload workbook
context: Sam Patel manages the AI, Data and Digital coaching teams. Rachel Moss has asked for a plan to clear {{fact:overdue_reviews}} overdue reviews and to know which coaches need caseload relief. The October Caseload Report holds coach capacity, Red learners and overdue reviews.
goal: Use Copilot in Excel to analyse the caseload workbook, identify the coaches and learners at greatest risk, and produce a short action summary for the Head of Delivery.
task_steps: Open Caseload Report — October 2026 in the Caseload Reports library.
On the Coaches sheet, ask Copilot to highlight coaches above 110% capacity and rank by overdue reviews.
On the Red learners sheet, ask Copilot to add a column showing how many OTJ hours each learner is short of 92% of expected.
Create a PivotTable or chart of Red learners and overdue reviews by academy.
Ask Copilot to list learners who are both Red and overdue for review.
Draft a 5-bullet summary for Rachel in Outlook or Word.
sample_prompts: Which coaches are above 110% capacity used? Sort by overdue reviews.
Add a column: OTJ hours needed to reach 92% of expected = 0.92 × OTJ expected − OTJ logged.
Show a chart of Red learners by academy.
Which learners appear on both the Red learners and Overdue reviews sheets?
Summarise the top three risks in this workbook for the Head of Delivery in five bullets.
success_criteria: Identifies AI Academy Reds correctly ({{fact:dlv_ai_red_learners}}) and Data Academy overdue reviews ({{fact:dlv_data_overdue}}).
Calculated column formula is correct and explained.
Cross-sheet list of Red and overdue learners is accurate.
Summary is concise, numeric and actionable.
trainer_notes: Learners may need to convert sheets to tables for Copilot in Excel. Check that they verify Copilot's counts with a filter or COUNTIFS.

title: Build a Coach Assistant agent
context: Fatima Hussain mentors new coaches, who ask the same questions every week: how often are reviews, what counts as OTJ, when do I escalate a Red, what's needed for gateway? The answers are spread across the Coach Handbook, Progress Review Procedure, Escalation Process, Gateway Checklist and the employer OTJ guide.
goal: Build a Copilot Studio agent, grounded on the Learning Delivery coaching resources, that answers coaches' process questions with citations; optionally extend it with an agent flow that emails coaches a list of their overdue reviews.
task_steps: Create a new agent in Copilot Studio called 'Coach Assistant'.

Add knowledge: the Coaching Resources library on the Learning Delivery site (Coach Handbook, Progress Review Procedure, At-Risk Learner Escalation Process, Gateway Readiness Checklist, OTJ guide, New Coach 30-60-90 Plan).
Write instructions (see reference) and add 4 starter prompts.
Test with the sample prompts and check citations are correct.
Stretch: build an agent flow, triggered weekly, that reads the Overdue reviews sheet and emails each coach their overdue list.
Publish to Teams for the 'Coaches – AI & Data' channel.
sample_prompts: How often do I need to hold a progress review, and when is the first one?
My learner has logged 180 of 240 expected OTJ hours. What's their RAG and what do I do?
Does Functional Skills study count as off-the-job training?
What do I need to check before submitting a learner for gateway?
What's my caseload target as a new coach at day 60?
success_criteria: Answers cite the correct source document.
Calculates RAG correctly (180/240 = 75% = Red) and states escalation within 5 working days.
Declines to answer questions about specific learners' safeguarding cases and signposts the DSL.
Stretch flow sends one email per coach with only their own learners.
agent_instructions: You are Coach Assistant, a helpful guide for Delcorn skills coaches. Answer questions about Delcorn's coaching processes — caseloads, 12-weekly tripartite progress reviews, off-the-job (OTJ) training rules, RAG ratings, escalation, breaks in learning and gateway — using ONLY the documents in the Learning Delivery Coaching Resources library. Always cite the document you used. When asked to rate progress, calculate OTJ logged ÷ OTJ expected and apply: Green ≥ 92%, Amber 78% to under 92%, Red under 78%; for Red, remind the coach to escalate to their delivery manager within 5 working days. Use UK English, be concise and practical, and give numbered steps for processes. Never give advice on individual safeguarding cases — direct the coach to the Designated Safeguarding Lead. If the documents don't cover the question, say so and suggest contacting the coach's delivery manager. Do not invent policy.
trainer_notes: Restrict knowledge to the Coaching Resources library to avoid surfacing confidential Learner Files. Discuss why the caseload workbook (Confidential) should not be general knowledge for this agent — the stretch flow should read it via a connector with the flow owner's permissions instead.
